To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stromal fibroblast cells, in a paracrine manner, induce the dedifferentiation of tumor cells to cancer stem cells, and that the dedifferentiation process can be blocked using exosomes’ mediated signaling inhibitors.
“Stromal fibroblats, under stress conditions, produce IL-6, Activin-A and G-CSF, which mediate dedifferentiation of tumor cells into cancer stem-like cells.”
“Stress-induced paracrine signaling from the tumor microenvironment drives tumor cell dedifferentiation and cancer stem cell generation”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation of CSCs and their therapeutic targeting.
a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying cancer development and progression.
the mechanisms underlying the formation of CSCs, their role in cancer progression and the potential of targeting these mechanisms for the treatment of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CSCs are a small population (0.1-1%) of resistant cells inhabitating the tumors.
the paracrine loop of cytokines secreted by the stromal fibroblast and tumor cell mediated by exosomes is a key factor for tumor formation.

the tumor stroma is not only a source of growth factors, cytokines and chemokines but also a major source of tumor cell dedifferentiation, a process that leads to tumor progression and resistance to chemotherapy and radiotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a mechanism by which cancer cells dedifferentiate into stem-like cells in response to hypoxic stress.
cancer stem cells can be generated from non-stem tumor cells by the action of cytokines and other soluble mediators secreted by the stromal microenvironment.
the stromal microenvironment can induce tumor cells’ dedifferentiation and the subsequent formation of a small population of cancer stem cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer stem cells may be generated by dedifferentiation, a process that can be blocked by targeting the cytokines involved in the process.
CSCs may arise from differentiated cells, which are not inherently stem cells.
CSCs may not be an intrinsic feature of the tumor cells but rather a result of the microenvironmental stress.
